question: Who was the brave and strategic founder of the great Maratha Empire? 🚩
explanation: Excellent! Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was the brilliant leader who carved out an independent Maratha kingdom using smart strategies and courage! 🚩
hint: He established his capital at Raigad and was crowned in 1674.

question: Who was the brave and inspiring mother of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj? 👩‍👦
explanation: Fantastic! Jijabai played a huge role in shaping Shivaji's character by telling him inspiring stories of heroes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata! 👩‍👦
hint: Her name starts with the letter 'J'.

question: What was the name of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's father? 🛡️
explanation: Brilliant! Shahaji Bhosale was a prominent Maratha general who served the Deccan Sultanates and was the father of Shivaji Maharaj! 🛡️
hint: His first name is Shahaji.

question: In which historical hill fort was Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj born? ⛰️
explanation: Awesome! Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was born in the majestic Shivneri fort, located near Pune! ⛰️
hint: The fort's name sounds very similar to his own name.

question: Who was the devoted guardian and teacher who trained young Shivaji in warfare and administration? 🏹
explanation: Great job! Dadoji Kondadev was his faithful guardian who taught young Shivaji essential military skills and how to govern people fairly! 🏹
hint: His first name starts with 'D'.

question: Which fort became the glorious capital of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's empire? 🏰
explanation: Perfect! Raigad was chosen as the capital because it was a strong, safe, and easily defensible hill fort! 🏰
hint: It was here that his grand coronation took place.

question: In which year did the grand coronation of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj take place? 🗓️
explanation: Spot on! The grand coronation took place in 1674, marking the official establishment of the independent Maratha Kingdom! 👑
hint: It happened exactly six years before he passed away in 1680.

question: What supreme title did Shivaji Maharaj assume during his coronation? 👑
explanation: Amazing! He assumed the title of 'Chhatrapati', which means the paramount sovereign or the lord of the royal umbrella! 👑
hint: This title became synonymous with Maratha kings.

question: What was the brilliant council of eight ministers created by Shivaji Maharaj called? 🧑‍⚖️
explanation: Excellent! The 'Ashtapradhan' was a council of eight wise ministers appointed to help him run the administration smoothly! 🧑‍⚖️
hint: The word 'Ashta' means eight in Sanskrit.

question: What was the title of the Prime Minister in the Ashtapradhan council? 📜
explanation: Wonderful! The Peshwa acted as the Prime Minister and was the most important minister in the Ashtapradhan! 📜
hint: This title later became the most powerful position in the Maratha Empire.

question: Which minister in the Ashtapradhan was responsible for managing the finances and accounts? 💰
explanation: Fantastic! The Amatya (or Majumdar) was the finance minister who kept a careful check on the kingdom's income and expenses! 💰
hint: The title starts with the letter 'A'.

question: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the mighty Maratha army in the Ashtapradhan? ⚔️
explanation: Great work! The Senapati (also called Sari Naubat) was the brave Commander-in-Chief who led the troops into battle! ⚔️
hint: The word 'Sena' means army.

question: Which minister handled foreign affairs and relationships with other kingdoms? 🤝
explanation: Spot on! The Sumant (or Dabir) was the foreign minister who expertly managed relationships with neighboring states! 🤝
hint: The title starts with the letter 'S' and ends with 't'.

question: Who was the head of justice in Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's administration? ⚖️
explanation: Brilliant! The Nyayadhish was the Chief Justice who ensured fair and equal justice for everyone in the kingdom! ⚖️
hint: The word 'Nyaya' means justice.

question: Which minister looked after religious matters and charities in the empire? 🕉️
explanation: Awesome! Pandit Rao was the minister dedicated to managing religious ceremonies, grants, and charities! 🕉️
hint: The title includes a word commonly used for a scholar or priest.

question: What smart military tactic did the Marathas use to defeat much larger armies? 🌳
explanation: Excellent! They used guerrilla warfare, a tactic of surprise attacks and quick retreats using the hilly terrain to their advantage! 🌳
hint: It involves hit-and-run strategies.

question: What was the traditional Marathi term used for guerrilla warfare tactics? 🗡️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Ganimi Kava' was the brilliant strategy of outsmarting the enemy through surprise attacks and mobility! 🗡️
hint: It starts with the word 'Ganimi'.

question: Who were the loyal and fearless foot soldiers from the western Ghats that formed the core of Shivaji's army? 🛡️
explanation: Wonderful! The Mavlas were extremely brave and agile soldiers from the Maval region who were fiercely loyal to Shivaji Maharaj! 🛡️
hint: They lived in the Maval region.

question: Which was one of the very first forts captured by young Shivaji Maharaj? 🏰
explanation: Great memory! Capturing the Torna fort at a very young age was one of his earliest and most exciting victories! 🏰
hint: The name starts with the letter 'T'.

question: Which powerful general of Bijapur was famously defeated by Shivaji Maharaj at Pratapgad? ⚔️
explanation: Spot on! Afzal Khan came to capture Shivaji, but Shivaji Maharaj cleverly outsmarted and defeated him at the Battle of Pratapgad! ⚔️
hint: His name begins with 'Afzal'.

question: What concealed weapon did Shivaji Maharaj use to protect himself and defeat Afzal Khan? 🐅
explanation: Brilliant! He secretly wore 'Bagh Nakh' (iron tiger claws) hidden in his hand to protect himself during the meeting! 🐅
hint: It is named after the sharp claws of a big striped cat.

question: Which Mughal general did Shivaji Maharaj surprise with a daring night attack in Pune? 🌙
explanation: Awesome! In a super daring move, Shivaji Maharaj and his men snuck into Shaista Khan's camp at night and forced him to flee Pune! 🌙
hint: He was the uncle of Emperor Aurangzeb.

question: Which skilled Rajput general did Aurangzeb send to fight against Shivaji Maharaj? 🐎
explanation: Excellent! Mirza Raja Jai Singh was a highly experienced general sent by Aurangzeb to besiege the Maratha forts! 🐎
hint: His name includes 'Mirza Raja'.

question: Which historic treaty was signed between Shivaji Maharaj and Jai Singh in 1665? 📜
explanation: Fantastic! The Treaty of Purandar was a strategic pause where Shivaji Maharaj agreed to hand over some forts to build future strength! 📜
hint: It is named after the Purandar fort.

question: In which city did Emperor Aurangzeb place Shivaji Maharaj under house arrest? 🏛️
explanation: Great job! Shivaji Maharaj visited Agra to meet the Emperor but was unfairly put under house arrest there! 🏛️
hint: This city is famous for the Taj Mahal.

question: How did Shivaji Maharaj make his legendary and clever escape from Agra? 🧺
options: Hidden in sweet and fruit baskets 🧺
answer: Hidden in sweet and fruit baskets 🧺
explanation: Spot on! He masterminded a brilliant escape by hiding himself and his son Sambhaji in large baskets meant for distributing sweets! 🧺
hint: Think of large containers used to carry tasty treats.

question: What was the tax representing one-fourth (1/4th) of the land revenue collected by the Marathas called? 💰
explanation: Brilliant! 'Chauth' meant one-fourth, and it was a tax collected from neighboring territories in exchange for Maratha protection! 💰
hint: The word sounds like 'one-fourth' in Hindi/Marathi.

question: What was the additional 10% tax collected by Shivaji Maharaj as the supreme head of the region? 👑
explanation: Awesome! 'Sardeshmukhi' was an extra 10% tax claimed by Shivaji Maharaj as the supreme leader (Sardeshmukh) of the land! 👑
hint: It contains the word 'Deshmukh'.

question: What was the royal seal of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj called? 📜
explanation: Excellent! The 'Rajmudra' was his glorious royal seal which promised that his rule was for the welfare of all people! 📜
hint: The word combines 'Raj' (royal) and 'Mudra' (seal).

question: In which classical language was the text on Shivaji Maharaj's Rajmudra written? 🕉️
explanation: Fantastic! Unusually for that time, he chose the ancient and respected language of Sanskrit for his beautiful royal seal! 🕉️
hint: It is known as the language of ancient Indian scriptures.

question: What was the name of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's legendary sword? ⚔️
explanation: Great work! His favorite and legendary sword was named 'Bhavani', representing power and divine blessing! ⚔️
hint: It is named after a powerful Goddess.

question: What type of structures were the backbone of the Maratha defense system? ⛰️
explanation: Spot on! The Marathas built and captured numerous hill forts, making it very difficult for enemies to attack them! ⛰️
hint: They were built high up in the Sahyadri mountains.

question: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj is known as the Father of the Indian _______ because of his coastal defenses. 🚢
explanation: Brilliant! He built a strong fleet of ships and naval forts like Sindhudurg to protect the coastline, earning him the title Father of the Indian Navy! 🚢
hint: It refers to armed forces on the sea.

question: Who was the famous and fierce admiral of the Maratha Navy? ⚓
explanation: Awesome! Kanhoji Angre was a brilliant naval commander who defended the Maratha coastline against foreign ships! ⚓
hint: His last name is Angre.

question: Who was a prominent saint and spiritual guide during Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's time? 🧘‍♂️
explanation: Excellent! Samarth Ramdas and Sant Tukaram were highly respected spiritual figures who inspired the people of Maharashtra! 🧘‍♂️
hint: His name includes 'Ramdas'.

question: Which modern-day Indian state is considered the historical heartland of the Maratha Empire? 🗺️
explanation: Fantastic! The great Maratha Empire originated in the hills and plains of present-day Maharashtra! 🗺️
hint: Mumbai is the capital of this state.

question: The fast and mobile part of the Maratha army, which rode on horses, was called the? 🐎
explanation: Great job! The Maratha cavalry (horse riders) was famous for its incredible speed, allowing them to strike quickly and disappear! 🐎
hint: Soldiers who fight on horseback.

question: Who succeeded Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj as the next Chhatrapati? 👑
explanation: Spot on! His brave eldest son, Sambhaji Maharaj, succeeded him and fiercely continued the fight against the Mughals! 👑
hint: He escaped with Shivaji Maharaj from Agra in a fruit basket.

question: After the capture of Sambhaji, who took charge and kept the Maratha resistance alive? 🛡️
explanation: Brilliant! Rajaram, Shivaji's younger son, bravely took over and led a powerful resistance against Aurangzeb! 🛡️
hint: His name has 'Raja' and 'Ram' in it.

question: Which courageous Maratha queen led the empire against Aurangzeb after the death of Rajaram? 👑
explanation: Awesome! Maharani Tarabai was an exceptionally brave queen who personally led the army and protected the empire from the Mughals! 👑
hint: Her name begins with 'T'.

question: Who became the Chhatrapati after being released from Mughal captivity following Aurangzeb's death? 🐎
explanation: Excellent! Shahu Maharaj returned and successfully claimed the Maratha throne, starting a new era of expansion! 🐎
hint: He was the son of Sambhaji.

question: During Chhatrapati Shahu's reign, the real power of the empire shifted into the hands of the _______. 📜
explanation: Fantastic! The Peshwas (Prime Ministers) became highly capable leaders who guided the empire to its greatest heights! 📜
hint: This was the title of the Prime Minister.

question: Which city became the bustling center of power during the era of the Peshwas? 🏛️
explanation: Great work! Pune flourished as the cultural and political headquarters of the Maratha Empire under the Peshwas! 🏛️
hint: Shaniwar Wada was built in this city.

question: Who was the highly capable first Peshwa appointed by Chhatrapati Shahu? ✍️
explanation: Spot on! Balaji Vishwanath was a very wise leader who restored order and made the Peshwa position powerful and hereditary! ✍️
hint: His first name is Balaji.

question: Which famous Peshwa is known for rapidly expanding the empire and never losing a single battle? ⚔️
explanation: Brilliant! Baji Rao I was a master of speed and cavalry tactics, winning every single battle he fought and greatly expanding the empire! ⚔️
hint: He is famously known as Baji Rao.

question: Under which Peshwa did the Maratha Empire reach its maximum territorial peak? 🗺️
explanation: Awesome! Balaji Baji Rao, also known as Nanasaheb, expanded the empire's borders all the way from the south to the northern parts of India! 🗺️
hint: His name combines the names of the first two Peshwas.

question: Which massive battle fought in 1761 temporarily halted the Maratha expansion in the north? 🛡️
explanation: Excellent! The Third Battle of Panipat was a huge clash that caused heavy losses, though the Marathas soon rebuilt their strength! 🛡️
hint: It was the third major battle fought in this town near Delhi.

question: Who was the Afghan invader that the Marathas fought against in the Third Battle of Panipat? 🗡️
explanation: Fantastic! Ahmad Shah Abdali, the ruler of Afghanistan, invaded India and was met by the brave Maratha army at Panipat! 🗡️
hint: His last name is Abdali.

question: In what year did the historic Third Battle of Panipat take place? 🗓️
explanation: Great job! The battle took place in 1761, a very important date in modern Indian history! 🗓️
hint: It happened in the 18th century, exactly in 1761.

question: What key advantage made the Maratha forces so difficult for larger armies to defeat? 🐎
explanation: Spot on! The Marathas were masters of speed! They traveled light, moved incredibly fast on horses, and surprised their enemies every time! 🐎
hint: It involves moving very quickly.
